description: Make Slack files explicitly attached to the current inbound message become SessionInput attachments via the existing provider-agnostic attachment boundary, fetched Server-side with honest per-file verdicts.

tasks.title: Slack file read primitives: adapter envelope + Server-side fetch
tasks.description: Add a `files` array (each `{id,name,mimetype,size}`) to the `mohist-slack` adapter's `SlackEnvelope`, parsed from the inbound Slack event without downloading content and without carrying `url_private`, bot token, or raw event payload. Add `ISlackApiClient.OpenFileContentAsync(fileId, botToken, ct)` that performs `files.info` + bearer-authenticated content download Server-side, returning a `SlackFileContent` (stream, filename, content-type, size). The adapter stays stateless and capped at `chat.postMessage`.
acceptanceCriteria: `SlackEnvelope.files` carries `{id,name,mimetype,size}` parsed from a Slack `message`/`file_share` event and contains no `url_private`, no bot token, and no raw event payload.
The adapter makes no Slack API call to fetch file content (unchanged `chat.postMessage`-only surface).

`ISlackApiClient.OpenFileContentAsync` returns content + authoritative metadata using the Connection's bot token; a 403/404/transport failure raises a not-readable error rather than returning partial data.
Unit tests cover adapter file extraction (including omission of secrets) and the API client against a faked HTTP handler for success, authorization failure (403), and not-found (404).
The 8 existing `ISlackApiClient` methods and existing adapter event handling are unchanged.
tasks.output: Updated `packages/mohist-slack/src/types.ts` + `adapter.ts`; updated `packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Slack/ISlackApiClient.cs` (+ response models) and `SlackApiClient.cs`; unit tests for both.
tasks.notes: Issue-516 precedent: Server owns all Slack reads via decrypted bot token; the download is a bearer-auth GET variant of the existing PostAsync auth path.

tasks.title: Provider-file ingest + source provenance in the attachment boundary
tasks.description: Add a nullable `Source` column to `AttachmentRow` (default `"upload"`) with an EF Core migration + backfill, add `AttachmentService.IngestProviderFileAsync(projectId, source, fileName, contentType, size, stream, ct)` as the Server-side analog of `UploadAsync` that writes a provider stream into a pending `AttachmentRow` and stamps its `Source`, and have `ToAgentInputDescriptor` read `row.Source` so accepted attachments expose their provenance.
acceptanceCriteria: EF migration adds `Attachments.Source` (nullable string); existing rows backfill to `"upload"`; the existing `UploadAsync` path stamps `"upload"`.

`IngestProviderFileAsync` writes bytes to `IAttachmentStorage`, creates a pending `AttachmentRow` (`OwnerKind=null`, `ExpiresAt=now+PendingTtl`) with the supplied `Source`, and enforces `MaxFileBytes` (rejects oversized before writing).
`ToAgentInputDescriptor` reads `row.Source`; an accepted attachment descriptor exposes the persisted source.

Unit tests verify ingest (pending row created with correct source + stored bytes), `MaxFileBytes` enforcement, and that the existing Web/CLI upload path still yields `Source = "upload"` with no regression.
Server build is warning-clean (`TreatWarningsAsErrors`).
tasks.output: Updated `AttachmentRow.cs`, new EF migration, `AttachmentService.cs` (new method + descriptor source read); unit tests.
tasks.notes: Provider-agnostic primitive — takes a stream, not Slack-specific. No production caller yet; T-003 is its first consumer.

tasks.title: Wire Slack files into connection launch + shared ingest-for-input helper + honest reply
tasks.description: Build the shared "Slack message -> accepted attachment descriptors" pipeline (premint deterministic owner ids from the message identity, pre-verdict size/type from the envelope, fetch via `OpenFileContentAsync`, ingest via `IngestProviderFileAsync`, `ValidateAndBindAgentInputAsync`, rollback newly-bound ids on downstream failure) and wire it into the DM-launch and channel-root-launch sites. Extend `AgentLauncher.LaunchConnectionAsync` to accept attachment descriptors + preminted ids and remove the empty-prompt guard (delegate to `EnsureInitialLaunch`'s text-or-attachment rule). Add `files` to `SlackIngressBody` and render the per-file verdict into the Bot acceptance reply via the existing outbox.
acceptanceCriteria: `LaunchConnectionAsync` accepts optional attachment descriptors + preminted session/input/turn ids and no longer rejects empty-prompt inputs; an input with neither text nor an accepted attachment is rejected by `EnsureInitialLaunch`.
A DM or channel-root message carrying a usable file and no text launches a new AgentSession with the file bound to the first SessionInput and `Source = "slack"`; no prompt is fabricated.

An oversized or unsupported file is rejected with its reason without any Slack content fetch; a file the Bot cannot read (403/download failure) is rejected `NotReadable`; each rejected file is reported, not silently dropped.
Redelivery of the same Slack launch message resolves to the same SessionInput and the same bound attachments with no duplicate fetch or bind (provider-inbox dedup + deterministic preminted owner).
The Bot acceptance reply names the accepted files and each rejected file with its concrete reason.

Spec tests cover DM-launch-files, channel-launch-files, attachment-only launch, per-file rejection (oversized/unsupported/Bot-unauthorized), launch redelivery idempotency, and Instructions/reply/transcript free of bot token, `url_private`, and raw event payload.
Server + runner build and the existing Web/CLI attachment spec tests remain green.
tasks.output: Updated `AgentLauncher.cs`, `SlackConnectionRoutes.cs` (DM-launch + channel-launch sites + `SlackIngressBody`), shared ingest-for-input helper, Bot reply rendering; spec + unit tests.
tasks.notes: Mirror `AgentSessionLaunchRoutes.cs:182-256` (premint + prebind + rollback). The launch coordinator envelope already has Attachments/PreMintedInputId/PreMintedTurnId slots. Build the helper here so T-004 reuses it.

tasks.title: Wire Slack files into connection follow-up (DM follow-up + thread reply)
tasks.description: Reuse the shared pipeline from T-003 to populate `RouteFollowupAsync` and the DM-follow-up / thread-reply-follow-up sites: premint the follow-up input id, fetch+ingest+bind Slack files via the helper, and pass accepted descriptors + preminted input id + per-file verdicts into `AcceptFollowupAsync` (its command already carries Attachments/PreMintedInputId/AttachmentResults). Render the per-file result in the follow-up Bot reply.
acceptanceCriteria: A DM follow-up or thread reply carrying a usable file and no text is accepted as a SessionInput with the file bound (`Source = "slack"`) and assigned to a Turn, with no fabricated prompt.
Per-file rejection (oversized/unsupported/Bot-unauthorized) is reported individually on the follow-up path; rejected files are not given to the Agent.

Redelivery of the same follow-up message resolves to the same SessionInput and bound attachments; after a restart that follows a durable accept, the message re-binds to the same preminted owner (no duplicate, no loss).
The Bot follow-up reply names accepted files and each rejected file with its reason.
Spec tests cover DM-followup-files, thread-reply-files, attachment-only follow-up, follow-up redelivery/restart idempotency, and honest per-file reply.
Server + runner build and all prior attachment spec tests remain green.
tasks.output: Updated `SlackConnectionRoutes.cs` (`RouteFollowupAsync` + DM-follow-up + thread-follow-up sites), follow-up Bot reply rendering; spec + unit tests.
tasks.notes: Mirror `AgentSessionFollowupRoutes.cs:146-195` (premint input id + prebind + AcceptFollowupAsync + rollback). Reuses the helper and reply renderer from T-003.
